children: Crude oil futures rose in a volatile session Thursday as a spate of Houthi attacks on Saudi targets raised fresh concerns of escalation in the Middle East.

A Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles ​fired by Iran-backed Houthis on Thursday, and Saudi Civil Defense issued an emergency alert warning in Mecca for potential danger; a Houthi spokesperson said his group launched dozens of missiles and drones against Saudi military targets in Jazan.

Iranian airlines were barred in neighboring countries, including the United Arab Emirates and Oman, in response to new U.S. sanctions, which prompted a threat to retaliate against neighboring countries that comply with the U.S. ban by making their airports "unusable."

"It certainly doesn't look as good as it did earlier in the week," Mizuho commodity specialist Robert Yawger said in a note. "The Iranians are threatening to take the battle to the Indian Ocean, and the Houthis are shooting ballistic missiles at Saudi cities."
However, U.S. and Iranian negotiators in New York reportedly are
out of war that would involve Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. lifting its economic blockade of Iran.
Energy shipments from Saudi Arabia through the Strait of Hormuz
to the highest level since the start of the Iran war, Bloomberg reported, after the country accelerated exports through the strait following the attack on its key East-West pipeline two weeks ago.
Saudi Arabia is said to be building up crude pumping volumes through the key pipeline that runs to its ​Red Sea export hub of Yanbu, although crude tanker loadings have yet to resume.
U.S. Central Command said in a social media post that its forces had redirected 115 commercial vessels as of Wednesday as part of its enforcement of the U.S. naval blockade on Iran.

"Continued Hormuz flows and a Saudi pipeline restart could ease physical supply pressures, but persistent tanker attacks and limited diplomatic progress should keep volatility and the geopolitical risk premium elevated," MUFG analyst Soojin Kim said in a note.

Meanwhile, the supply of diesel and other refined products remains tight, and most analysts say a potential full or partial U.S. diesel export ban would provide only limited short-term relief and could eventually
Front-month Nymex crude
for November delivery closed 2.6% higher at $94.61/bbl, and front-month Brent November crude
jumped 3.4% to $106.60/bbl, its highest settlement since September 15.

However, U.S. futures for oil products took a rest, as front-month Nymex ultra-low-sulfur diesel (HO1:COM) for October delivery fell 1% to $4.7303/gal, and front-month Nymex RBOB October gasoline (XB1:COM) slipped 0.6% to $3.5646/gal.
U.S. natural gas futures
surged by the most since January after TC Energy

declared force majeure on a gas pipeline in West Virginia after detecting a leak at the Saunders Creek Regulator Station; the front-month Nymex October contract gained 9% to $3.297/MMBtu, its highest settlement value since June 25.
